source.title: Discovering Interpretable Biological Concepts in Single-cell RNA-seq Foundation Models
source.authors: C. Claye; P. Marschall; Wassila Ouerdane; Céline Hudelot; Julien Duquesne

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or wrong-document issue. Some figure content is flattened, and the relevant comparison does not state exact values in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures expert and pathway-based interpretability of individual neurons, but neither measure tests whether a neuron responds to unrelated inputs or whether those inputs share a feature. Its results concern an adjacent construct, interpretability, rather than the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly compares neurons with SAE concepts and states that concepts are more interpretable. The relevant neuron results are shown in Figure 3, but the text gives no exact neuron counts or rates. They do not establish whether neuron activations mix unrelated inputs. Other results on SAE reconstruction, concept stability, and downstream classification do not test the listed versions and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on scRNA-seq model cell embeddings (scGPT CLS token, scVI latent) and compares interpretability of SAE concepts with individual embedding dimensions via one expert and pathway enrichment. It never measures whether a neuron responds to unrelated inputs, in vision or language models, nor causes, architecture effects, or measurement dependence. 'Not interpretable' neurons are not shown to be polysemantic, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude SAE concepts are more interpretable than individual neurons for scGPT and scVI, preserve signal in downstream classification (accuracy 0.86 vs 0.87 and 0.49 vs 0.48), and include some concepts stable across datasets. They make no claim about neurons responding to unrelated inputs.
record.recipe_differences: The study extracts Topk SAE concepts from scRNA-seq cell embeddings and compares their interpretability with individual neurons; it does not apply the original vision-neuron analysis or measure mixed-input responses.

fits_no_version.finding: In scGPT and scVI embeddings, a single expert and attribution-based GSEA judged 20 random SAE concepts more interpretable and more pathway-aligned than 20 random embedding dimensions. About half of the concepts remained uninterpretable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In single-cell RNA-seq foundation models, SAE concepts are more interpretable than individual embedding dimensions.

record.problems: The expert interpretation study used one domain expert and 20 randomly selected neurons per model. The paper does not state exact neuron annotation values in the text, and interpretability annotations do not directly establish polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: Results on SAE scales, reconstruction, concept stability, deletion curves, and downstream classification were omitted because they do not measure neuron responses to unrelated inputs or test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: All: no vision classifier neurons studied.
All: no transformer MLP neurons; only the scGPT final CLS embedding; no share or layer distribution.
All: SAEs are used, but superposition as a cause is not tested.
All: no comparison of activation function or regularization on the neuron polysemanticity share.
All: neurons are not examined for a shared underlying feature.
All: only the top-10 activating cells are used; activation range and scoring are not varied.

record.verdict_notes: Several features of the design limit any reading toward polysemanticity: the 'neurons' are output embedding dimensions, the expert study used one expert and 20 units per model, and no polysemanticity metric is reported. Appendix-level logistic-regression neuron examples (Fig 5B) show high-coefficient neurons that are not task-relevant. This too is interpretability, not mixed-response evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Vision models, including InceptionV1, and mixed visual inputs.
The share and layer distribution of polysemantic MLP neurons in language models.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
Polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
Whether architecture, activation, or regularization changes the share of polysemantic neurons, or lowers it without large performance loss.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons detect a shared feature or related jobs rather than unrelated mixtures.
Whether polysemanticity depends on activation range or explanation scoring.

relation.reason: It doesn't test polysemanticity. Neurons appear only as an interpretability comparator for SAE concepts.

tranche.reason: It compares how interpretable SAE concepts and individual embedding dimensions are in scRNA-seq models (scGPT, scVI). It never measures whether a neuron responds to unrelated inputs, and it never mentions polysemanticity.

source_check.notes: The 'neurons' are scGPT CLS-token embedding dimensions (d=512) and scVI VAE latent dimensions (d=50), not vision or LM MLP neurons. Neuron values are figure-only (Fig 3.A). Interpretability is not polysemanticity. The text states the 20-neuron sample only for the expert study, not for pathway enrichment (Fig 3.A.b plots ratios).
